purpose: Symptom-to-cause corpus for FDM fault diagnosis, written for a competent technician on a maintained machine.

rankingModel.base: Each cause carries a baseWeight. Selecting several symptoms accumulates weight for causes that explain more than one (subsequent hits add at 0.75x).

contextFlags.hygro: x1.35 for hygroscopic materials, x0.75 otherwise
contextFlags.abrasive: x1.3 for filled materials, x0.7 otherwise; a further x1.4 when nozzle wear exceeds 80% of expected bore life
contextFlags.needsChamber: x1.4 when the material wants a chamber and the printer has no active heater
contextFlags.mech: x0.55 always - mechanical causes are deliberately demoted on a maintained fleet
contextFlags.multi: x1.3 on a multi-material machine, x0.6 otherwise
contextFlags.drift: x1.45 when onset is gradual, x0.7 when sudden
contextFlags.sudden: x1.4 when onset is sudden, x0.85 otherwise

rankingModel.newCombination: drift and sudden causes are both x0.6 when the user reports the combination never worked

symptoms.label: Stringing and oozing
symptoms.hint: Fine strands between islands

causes.cause: Moisture in the filament
causes.why: Absorbed water flashes to steam in the melt zone and drives filament out of the nozzle during travel. It is the single most common cause of stringing on a machine whose retraction is already tuned.

fixes.action: Dry at the material\'s drying temperature for the full cycle, then re-run the same print without touching retraction
Extrude 100 mm in air and listen — steam ticking or a wandering strand confirms it

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print a two-tower retraction test straight after drying. If stringing is gone, the parameters were never wrong.

causes.cause: Nozzle temperature above the material's flow window
causes.why: Lower viscosity means the melt drains under its own head pressure faster than retraction can hold it.

fixes.action: nozzle_temperature, keeping the first layer where it is
repeat if strings persist and layer adhesion still passes a snap test

causes.nextDiagnostic: Temperature tower in 5 °C steps across the material range, judged on strings and on layer bonding together.

causes.cause: Retraction too short for this melt-zone volume
causes.why: Retraction has to unload the compressed melt column. A larger melt zone stores more, so a value tuned on one hotend does not transfer to another.

fixes.action: filament_retraction_length, to a ceiling of about 1.5 mm on direct drive
filament_retraction_speed if the extruder is not skipping

causes.nextDiagnostic: Retraction tower, 0.4 → 1.4 mm. Stop at the first value that is clean; longer is not better and invites clogs.

causes.cause: Travel avoiding the wipe
causes.why: Without a wipe move the pressure that remains after retraction lands on the next seam as a strand.

fixes.action: filament_wipe
filament_wipe_distance

causes.nextDiagnostic: Slice one layer and inspect the travel preview for retract-then-move ordering.

causes.cause: Partially blocked nozzle
causes.why: A partial obstruction raises the pressure the retraction has to relieve and leaves residual ooze even at correct settings.

fixes.action: Two cold pulls at the material's softening point, then inspect the tip
Swap the nozzle if the pulls come out with carbon flecks

causes.nextDiagnostic: Weigh a 100 mm extrusion at a known flow. Under-delivery of more than 4% points at the nozzle, not the settings.

symptoms.label: Blobs, zits and seam bulges
symptoms.hint: Raised dots on the outer wall

causes.cause: Pressure advance too low
causes.why: Without enough advance the extruder does not unload before a stop, so the residual pressure deposits at the seam.

fixes.action: pressure advance / k factor
Bambu flow-dynamics calibration for this specific spool, not the SKU

causes.nextDiagnostic: PA pattern test. Read the line where the corner deposit disappears without the corner going hollow.

causes.cause: Seam placement on a visible face
causes.why: The seam is a real artefact of a stop-start; moving it is cheaper than eliminating it.

fixes.action: filament_scarf_seam_type to a scarf joint
Set seam painting to a rear or internal edge

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print the same wall with scarf seam on and off, side by side.

causes.cause: Retraction restart extra overfeeding
causes.why: Restart extra compensates for ooze; when ooze is already controlled it becomes an over-extrusion at every restart.

fixes.action: filament_retract_restart_extra

causes.nextDiagnostic: Single-wall vase print — restart artefacts show up unmistakably.

causes.cause: Wet filament boiling at the seam pause
causes.why: Dwell time at the seam gives steam a moment to form a bubble that bursts as the head moves off.

fixes.action: Full drying cycle before touching PA

causes.nextDiagnostic: Compare a seam close-up before and after drying.

symptoms.label: Corner bulging
symptoms.hint: Walls fatten at direction changes

causes.cause: Pressure advance too low
causes.why: The melt column stays compressed through the deceleration, so the slow-moving nozzle lays down more material than the geometry asks for.

fixes.action: k factor, then bisect
Flow-dynamics calibration per spool

causes.nextDiagnostic: PA line test at your actual print acceleration — PA measured at a different acceleration will not transfer.

causes.cause: Acceleration set higher than the PA value was tuned at
causes.why: Advance compensation scales with the rate of velocity change; retuning acceleration invalidates the k factor.

fixes.action: Re-run PA calibration at the acceleration the profile actually uses

causes.nextDiagnostic: Note the acceleration on the calibration print so the pair stays together.

causes.cause: Over-extrusion masking as a corner defect
causes.why: If flow ratio is high everywhere, corners are simply where it becomes visible first.

fixes.action: filament_flow_ratio

causes.nextDiagnostic: Single-wall cube, measure the wall with a micrometer at mid-height and compare to line width.

symptoms.label: Under-extrusion, gaps between lines
symptoms.hint: Visible voids in walls and top

causes.cause: Commanded flow above the hotend's melt ceiling
causes.why: Past the melt rate the hotend can supply, the extruder skips or the melt leaves the nozzle short. This is the ceiling the Recommend tab computes.

fixes.action: filament_max_volumetric_speed to the computed ceiling for this hotend and nozzle
nozzle_temperature if there is headroom in the material range

causes.nextDiagnostic: Run the flow-rate test in the Recommend tab's derivation, then record the measured value against the spool.

causes.cause: Worn nozzle bore
causes.why: An abraded orifice goes oval and oversize; the slicer's line width no longer matches what the nozzle lays down, and the deficit shows as gaps.

fixes.action: Fit a fresh nozzle of the same size and class
Record kilograms through the nozzle in the Hotends tab

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print a single-wall cube before and after the swap and measure both. A width change of more than 0.03 mm confirms wear.

causes.cause: Partial clog
causes.why: Carbonised material narrows the bore and throttles flow before the extruder complains.

fixes.action: Cold pull twice, then a purge at 20 °C above normal
Replace if pulls come out discoloured

causes.nextDiagnostic: Weigh 100 mm of extrusion at a known volumetric rate; compare to filament cross-section × length × density.

causes.cause: Flow ratio calibrated on a different batch
causes.why: Diameter tolerance and pigment loading vary lot to lot; a flow ratio is a per-batch number, not a per-brand one.

fixes.action: filament_flow_ratio for this batch
Ten diameter readings along a metre of filament

causes.nextDiagnostic: Flow calibration cube for this batch, then store the value against the batch in the library.

causes.cause: Extruder gear slipping on soft or dusty filament
causes.why: Grip loss delivers less than the commanded length without any error being raised.

fixes.action: Clean the drive gear teeth
commanded flow while testing whether skipping stops

causes.nextDiagnostic: Mark the filament 100 mm above the entry, command 100 mm, measure what actually fed.

symptoms.label: Over-extrusion, rough top, elephant foot
symptoms.hint: Surfaces proud, first layer squashed wide

causes.cause: Flow ratio high for this batch
causes.why: Flow ratio is the direct multiplier on extruded volume; a batch with slightly oversize filament pushes more than the model assumes.

fixes.action: filament_flow_ratio
Filament diameter at ten points and set filament_diameter to the mean

causes.nextDiagnostic: Flow calibration cube; measure the top surface flatness rather than the wall.

causes.cause: First-layer squish set for a different plate
causes.why: Textured, engineering and Supertack plates sit at different effective heights; a Z offset tuned on one over-squashes on another.

fixes.action: Z offset for the plate actually installed
the plate-specific bed temperature key

causes.nextDiagnostic: First-layer patch test on the plate in use.

causes.cause: Nozzle temperature high enough to slump the bead
causes.why: An over-hot bead spreads after deposition and reads as over-extrusion even at correct flow.

fixes.action: nozzle_temperature

causes.nextDiagnostic: Temperature tower judged on top-surface finish.

symptoms.label: Poor layer adhesion, parts split under load
symptoms.hint: Clean break along a layer line

causes.cause: Cooling too aggressive for the material
causes.why: Interlayer strength is diffusion across the weld, and diffusion needs time above the glass transition. Fan robs exactly that time.

fixes.action: fan_max_speed and fan_min_speed
overhang_fan_speed, accepting softer overhangs

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print two identical tensile bars at the current and reduced fan, and break both.

causes.cause: Nozzle temperature at the bottom of the window
causes.why: Weld strength rises steeply with melt temperature until degradation sets in. Most adhesion complaints are a 15 °C problem.

fixes.action: nozzle_temperature, staying inside nozzle_temperature_range_high
again if the break is still along the layer

causes.nextDiagnostic: Temperature tower broken by hand at each step rather than inspected visually.

causes.cause: Chamber too cold for an amorphous engineering polymer
causes.why: Below the material's glass transition the previous layer has already vitrified when the next arrives, so the weld never forms properly.

fixes.action: chamber_temperatures toward the material's guidance
Door and top closed for the whole print, not just the start

causes.nextDiagnostic: Same part, chamber cold versus hot, broken and compared.

causes.cause: Moisture degrading the weld
causes.why: Hydrolysis shortens polymer chains in polyesters and polyamides; the material extrudes but never regains strength.

fixes.action: Full drying cycle, then print from a heated or desiccated feed

causes.nextDiagnostic: Break a bar printed from dried stock against one from the open spool.

causes.cause: Line width too narrow to bond
causes.why: A thin bead has less contact area with the layer below.

fixes.action: line width for a 0.4 nozzle
layer height for the same effect

causes.nextDiagnostic: Compare bars at 0.42 and 0.48 mm width.

symptoms.label: Warping and corner lift
symptoms.hint: Part peels from the plate at corners

causes.cause: Chamber below the material's glass transition
causes.why: Every layer contracts as it cools through Tg. If the part sits far below Tg, that contraction accumulates as internal stress with nowhere to go but the corners.

fixes.action: chamber_temperatures to within 40–60 °C of the material's Tg where the printer allows
Close the machine and let it soak before starting

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print the same footprint with the chamber cold and hot; measure corner lift with feeler gauges.

causes.cause: Bed temperature below the material's Tg at the first layer
causes.why: The plate has to hold the base layers above their softening point or the anchor releases before the print finishes.

fixes.action: the plate-specific bed temperature key in use
hot_plate_temp_initial_layer to the running bed temperature

causes.nextDiagnostic: Adhesion patch test at three bed temperatures.

causes.cause: Cooling fan running on a warp-prone material
causes.why: Fan accelerates the contraction that causes the stress.

fixes.action: fan_max_speed
close_fan_the_first_x_layers or more

causes.nextDiagnostic: Same part with fan disabled entirely as the control.

causes.cause: Footprint geometry concentrating stress
causes.why: Sharp corners and thin footprints have the smallest anchor area per unit of accumulated stress.

fixes.action: Add a brim of at least 5 mm
Fillet base corners in CAD if the design allows

causes.nextDiagnostic: Add a brim as a diagnostic — if lift stops, the problem is anchoring, not thermal.

causes.cause: Plate contamination
causes.why: Skin oils are the usual culprit and defeat an otherwise correct thermal setup.

fixes.action: Hot water and dish soap, not isopropyl alone, then dry fully

causes.nextDiagnostic: Wash and repeat the identical print before changing any parameter.

symptoms.label: Cracking or delamination on tall parts
symptoms.hint: Splits appear well above the plate

causes.cause: Thermal gradient up the build height
causes.why: The base sits in warm air near the bed while the top cools in a colder zone. The accumulated differential shear finally exceeds the weld strength at some height.

fixes.action: chamber_temperatures and let the machine soak for 15 minutes before the print
bed temperature slightly once the chamber is hot, to flatten the gradient

causes.nextDiagnostic: Log chamber temperature against build height on a failed print; the crack usually sits at the gradient knee.

causes.cause: Fan cycling on small upper layers
causes.why: As cross-section shrinks the cooling logic raises fan and lowers speed, quenching exactly the layers that are already weakest.

fixes.action: fan_max_speed
reduce_fan_stop_start_freq
slow_down_layer_time so the slowdown starts earlier and more gently

causes.nextDiagnostic: Inspect the slicer's per-layer fan preview at the crack height.

causes.cause: Interlayer weld marginal from the start
causes.why: A weld that only just holds at the bottom fails first where stress is highest.

fixes.action: nozzle_temperature
line width

causes.nextDiagnostic: Snap test on a short specimen before committing to a tall print.

symptoms.label: First layer not sticking
symptoms.hint: Lines lift or drag behind the nozzle

causes.cause: Wrong plate temperature key active
causes.why: Bambu profiles carry separate temperatures for cool, engineering, textured and Supertack plates. Editing one leaves the others untouched, and the slicer uses whichever plate is selected.

fixes.action: All four plate keys, or at minimum the one for the plate installed

causes.nextDiagnostic: Check the plate selected in the slicer against the plate on the machine.

causes.cause: Plate contamination
causes.why: Release agents and skin oils survive an isopropyl wipe.

fixes.action: Hot water and detergent, air dry, handle by the edges afterwards

causes.nextDiagnostic: Wash and repeat the identical file with no other change.

causes.cause: First layer moving too fast for the melt to wet the plate
causes.why: Adhesion is a wetting process and wetting takes contact time.

fixes.action: first layer speed
nozzle_temperature_initial_layer

causes.nextDiagnostic: First-layer patch test at two speeds.

causes.cause: Z offset drift
causes.why: A knocked plate or a changed nozzle shifts the datum even on a machine that self-levels.

fixes.action: Run bed levelling and the Z offset routine after any nozzle change

causes.nextDiagnostic: Run levelling, then a patch test before assuming a material problem.

symptoms.label: Ringing and ghosting
symptoms.hint: Echo of a corner repeated along the wall

causes.cause: Acceleration or jerk above what input shaping was calibrated for
causes.why: Input shaping cancels one resonance at one set of dynamics; raising acceleration moves the excitation outside what the filter was fitted to.

fixes.action: Re-run vibration compensation, then keep acceleration where it was measured
outer wall acceleration only, leaving infill alone

causes.nextDiagnostic: Ringing tower at three accelerations.

causes.cause: Pressure advance overshoot at corners
causes.why: An over-set k factor injects a velocity transient of its own that looks like mechanical ringing.

fixes.action: k factor

causes.nextDiagnostic: PA test — mechanical ringing repeats at a fixed spatial period, PA artefacts do not.

causes.cause: Spool binding on the holder
causes.why: A jerky feed excites the toolhead through the extruder. Rare, but it is the mechanical cause that survives good maintenance.

fixes.action: Spool spins freely; no tangle under the top wrap

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print with the filament hand-fed from a loose coil as a control.

symptoms.label: Poor overhangs, drooping
symptoms.hint: Underside of overhangs curls or sags

causes.cause: Overhang cooling not aggressive enough
causes.why: An unsupported bead has to freeze before the next one lands on it. Bambu exposes a separate overhang fan speed and threshold for exactly this.

fixes.action: overhang_fan_speed toward 100%
overhang_fan_threshold so more of the wall counts as overhang

causes.nextDiagnostic: Overhang test wedge at two fan settings.

causes.cause: Overhang speed too high
causes.why: The bead needs dwell time in front of the fan. Bambu's per-quarter overhang speed keys exist to slow only the unsupported portion.

fixes.action: filament_overhang_3_4_speed and filament_overhang_4_4_speed
filament_enable_overhang_speed

causes.nextDiagnostic: Compare the same wedge with overhang speed control on and off.

causes.cause: Nozzle temperature high for the cooling available
causes.why: A hotter bead takes longer to freeze; on an enclosed machine with limited fan this becomes the binding constraint.

fixes.action: nozzle_temperature for the overhang region

causes.nextDiagnostic: Temperature tower judged on the overhang face only.

symptoms.label: Bridging sags or fails
symptoms.hint: Spans between supports drop

causes.cause: Bridge speed and flow mismatched
causes.why: A bridge is a stretched, unsupported filament — it wants slightly less material and constant velocity.

fixes.action: filament_bridge_speed toward 25–40 mm/s
bridge flow

causes.nextDiagnostic: Bridge test at three speeds over the longest span in the real part.

causes.cause: Insufficient cooling on the bridge layer
causes.why: The span has to freeze in flight; without full fan it never does.

fixes.action: fan on bridge layers

causes.nextDiagnostic: Same bridge test with fan forced to full.

causes.cause: Material simply too soft for the span
causes.why: High-Tg engineering materials printed in a hot chamber stay compliant longer and bridge worse than PLA ever will.

fixes.action: Accept supports for spans past 20 mm on chamber-heated materials

causes.nextDiagnostic: Bridge the same span in PLA as a control to separate material from settings.

symptoms.label: Top surface pinholes
symptoms.hint: Top layer does not close

causes.cause: Flow ratio slightly low
causes.why: Top surfaces are the least forgiving place for a flow deficit because there is no wall to hide it.

fixes.action: filament_flow_ratio

causes.nextDiagnostic: Flow calibration cube judged on the top face.

causes.cause: Not enough top solid layers for the layer height
causes.why: Solid thickness, not layer count, is what closes a surface.

fixes.action: top solid layers, or raise until top thickness reaches about 0.8 mm

causes.nextDiagnostic: Slice preview of the top layers over sparse infill.

causes.cause: Ironing masking a flow problem
causes.why: Ironing can hide pinholes at low speed while leaving the underlying deficit in place.

fixes.action: Turn ironing off while diagnosing, then re-enable

causes.nextDiagnostic: Judge the surface with ironing disabled.

symptoms.label: Popping, steam, bubbly surface
symptoms.hint: Audible ticking, rough matte finish

causes.cause: Absorbed moisture
causes.why: Water boils in the melt zone and leaves voids and a matte, fuzzy surface. In polyamides and polyesters it also cuts chains and drops strength permanently.

fixes.action: Run the material's full drying cycle before anything else
Print from a heated chamber or desiccated dry box for hygroscopic grades

causes.nextDiagnostic: Extrude 100 mm in still air and watch for steam and bubbles. This is a two-minute confirmation.

causes.cause: Contamination or a mixed-material clog
causes.why: Residue from a higher-temperature material degrading in the melt zone gives a similar crackle.

fixes.action: Purge 200 mm at the higher material's temperature, then cold pull

causes.nextDiagnostic: Inspect the purge for discoloured flecks.

symptoms.label: Filament snaps in the tube or on the spool
symptoms.hint: Breaks during feeding or AMS retract

causes.cause: Hydrolytic degradation from long humid storage
causes.why: Polyesters and polyamides lose molecular weight when stored wet. Drying restores printability but does not undo the chain scission.

fixes.action: Dry, then test — if it still snaps the spool is spent
Retire the spool for structural work

causes.nextDiagnostic: Bend a 100 mm length around a 50 mm radius. Clean snap means retire it.

causes.cause: Tight winding stress on a small-core spool
causes.why: Filament that has been held at a small bend radius for a long time embrittles at the outer wrap.

fixes.action: Discard the outer few metres

causes.nextDiagnostic: Compare the outer wrap against material from mid-spool.

symptoms.label: Extruder clicking or grinding
symptoms.hint: Ticking sound, flat spot on the filament

causes.cause: Commanded flow above what the melt zone can supply
causes.why: The extruder is pushing against a pressure it cannot overcome, so the gear slips. The Recommend tab computes both the flow ceiling and the force required.

fixes.action: filament_max_volumetric_speed to the computed ceiling
nozzle_temperature to drop melt viscosity

causes.nextDiagnostic: Repeat the same print at 70% flow. If clicking stops, it was flow, not hardware.

causes.cause: Partial clog raising back-pressure
causes.why: A restriction multiplies the force needed for the same flow.

fixes.action: Cold pull, then a hot purge
Replace the nozzle if the pull shows carbon

causes.nextDiagnostic: Free-air extrusion at 5 mm³/s — if that clicks too, it is the nozzle, not the print.

causes.cause: Too much retraction on a soft material
causes.why: Retracting a flexible filament buckles it in the drive rather than pulling melt back.

fixes.action: filament_retraction_length for TPU grades
filament_retraction_speed

causes.nextDiagnostic: Retraction tower on the flexible material specifically.

causes.cause: Heat creep softening filament above the melt zone
causes.why: Softened filament swells in the cold side and jams. It shows up on long prints in a hot chamber.

fixes.action: chamber temperature if the material tolerates it
Hotend fan running at full for the whole print

causes.nextDiagnostic: Note whether failures cluster after a consistent elapsed time — that signature is heat creep, not settings.

symptoms.label: Flow fades then recovers mid-print
symptoms.hint: Bands of thin extrusion

causes.cause: Intermittent partial clog
causes.why: A fragment cycles between blocking and clearing as pressure builds and releases.

fixes.action: Several cold pulls until the pulled tip is clean and sharp
Replace the nozzle — intermittent clogs rarely clear for good

causes.nextDiagnostic: Watch extrusion width in the first 20 layers after a nozzle swap.

causes.cause: Heat creep on long prints
causes.why: Warm-side temperature climbs through the print until the filament softens above the melt zone.

fixes.action: Hotend cooling fan speed and airflow path
chamber temperature where the material allows

causes.nextDiagnostic: Log the elapsed time at each fade. A repeatable interval points at thermal, not material.

causes.cause: Filament diameter variation within the spool
causes.why: An out-of-tolerance section under-delivers volume until it passes through.

fixes.action: Diameter every 200 mm across several metres
filament_diameter to the measured mean

causes.nextDiagnostic: Correlate the band spacing with spool circumference — a match points at the spool, not the machine.

symptoms.label: Complete blockage, no extrusion
symptoms.hint: Extruder skipping, nothing comes out

causes.cause: Carbonised deposit in the melt zone
causes.why: Long dwell at temperature, especially after a high-temperature material, bakes residue onto the bore.

fixes.action: Heat to print temperature, cool to the softening point, pull firmly
Replace the nozzle if two pulls do not clear it

causes.nextDiagnostic: Inspect the pulled tip under magnification — a clean cone means the melt zone is clear.

causes.cause: Material change without an adequate purge
causes.why: A high-temperature residue will not move at the new material's temperature and blocks the path.

fixes.action: Purge at the higher of the two materials' temperatures before switching down

causes.nextDiagnostic: Standardise a purge volume when stepping down in temperature.

causes.cause: Foreign particle from the spool
causes.why: Dust and swarf collected on the filament path end up in the nozzle.

fixes.action: Fit a filament dust wiper
Replace the nozzle

causes.nextDiagnostic: Check whether the same spool blocks a second nozzle.

symptoms.label: Extrusion width wanders, dimensions drift
symptoms.hint: Same file prints differently week to week

causes.cause: Nozzle bore wear
causes.why: Filled materials abrade the orifice steadily. The bore grows and goes out of round, so the actual line width no longer matches the commanded one.

fixes.action: Fit a fresh nozzle; use hardened steel or carbide for any filled grade
Record kilograms through each nozzle so replacement is scheduled, not reactive

causes.nextDiagnostic: Single-wall cube measured with a micrometer, logged per nozzle. A drift past 0.03 mm is the replacement trigger.

causes.cause: Batch-to-batch filament diameter variation
causes.why: Nominal 1.75 mm covers a real spread, and pigment loading changes it further.

fixes.action: Ten readings per new spool
filament_diameter and filament_flow_ratio per batch, stored against the batch

causes.nextDiagnostic: Log measured diameter against batch in the library and compare across lots.

causes.cause: Ambient temperature swing
causes.why: Shrinkage compensation is calibrated at one ambient; a workshop that swings 10 °C moves finished dimensions.

fixes.action: filament_shrink against parts measured at a stable ambient

causes.nextDiagnostic: Measure the same calibration part at both ends of the daily temperature range.

symptoms.label: Holes undersize, dimensions off
symptoms.hint: Parts do not fit assemblies

causes.cause: Hole compensation coefficients not tuned for this material
causes.why: Bambu carries per-filament polynomial compensation for holes and outer contours; it is a material property, not a machine one.

fixes.action: hole_coef_2 and hole_coef_3 against measured holes
counter_coef_2 and counter_coef_3 for outer contours

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print a gauge plate with holes from 3 to 20 mm, measure with pin gauges, fit the correction.

causes.cause: Shrinkage not set for the material
causes.why: Semi-crystalline materials shrink far more than PLA, and the amount depends on chamber temperature.

fixes.action: filament_shrink from measured parts at the chamber temperature you actually run

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print a 100 mm bar, measure cold, set the ratio from the result.

causes.cause: Over- or under-extrusion shifting every surface
causes.why: Flow error moves outer walls out and holes in, symmetrically.

fixes.action: filament_flow_ratio before touching any compensation coefficient

causes.nextDiagnostic: Flow first, dimensions second. Compensations fitted on top of a flow error will not transfer.

causes.cause: Elephant foot on the seating face
causes.why: A squashed first layer reads as an oversize base in every measurement taken from it.

fixes.action: Elephant foot compensation
Z offset for the plate in use

causes.nextDiagnostic: Measure at mid-height and at the base separately to separate the two effects.

symptoms.label: Z banding, periodic horizontal lines
symptoms.hint: Regular bands at a fixed pitch

causes.cause: Flow pulsation from filament diameter variation
causes.why: A diameter cycle from the extrusion line prints as a band whose pitch matches the spool geometry.

fixes.action: Diameter along several metres; look for a repeating cycle

causes.nextDiagnostic: Compare band pitch against the layers printed per spool revolution.

causes.cause: Temperature oscillation around the setpoint
causes.why: A worn or loose thermistor or heater lets the PID hunt, and viscosity follows it.

fixes.action: Log nozzle temperature during a print and look for swing beyond ±2 °C
Re-run hotend PID tuning

causes.nextDiagnostic: Temperature log across ten minutes of steady printing.

causes.cause: Lead screw or Z artefact
causes.why: On a maintained machine this is unlikely, but a band pitch exactly matching the Z screw lead is diagnostic.

fixes.action: Band pitch against the Z lead

causes.nextDiagnostic: If the pitch matches the screw lead exactly, it is mechanical; otherwise it is not.

symptoms.label: Layer shift
symptoms.hint: Print offsets partway up

causes.cause: Collision with a curled part or lifted corner
causes.why: On a maintained machine the overwhelmingly common shift is the toolhead hitting something the print itself created.

fixes.action: Z hop, and set filament_z_hop_types to a spiral or slope lift
Address the warping first — see corner lift

causes.nextDiagnostic: Inspect the part at the shift height for a raised edge on the side the shift moved toward.

causes.cause: Acceleration above what the part mass supports
causes.why: A tall part with a small footprint can be knocked by its own inertia.

fixes.action: acceleration for tall parts

causes.nextDiagnostic: Reprint at reduced acceleration as the control.

causes.cause: Belt or carriage fault
causes.why: Listed last deliberately — on a serviced machine this is rare, and the two causes above account for most shifts.

fixes.action: Belt tension and carriage play at the next scheduled service

causes.nextDiagnostic: Only pursue after collision and acceleration have been excluded.

symptoms.label: Colour or gloss differs between batches
symptoms.hint: Same SKU, visibly different parts

causes.cause: Pigment loading varies between lots
causes.why: Pigment changes both the melt rheology and the surface reflectivity. It is a real property of the batch, not an error.

fixes.action: Store the batch code against every spool and keep matched batches for one job
filament_flow_ratio per batch — heavily pigmented lots often need a different value

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print a swatch from each batch under the same settings and keep them with the spools.

causes.cause: Different effective print temperature
causes.why: Gloss on many materials tracks melt temperature closely; 10 °C is visible.

fixes.action: nozzle_temperature across the batches being mixed

causes.nextDiagnostic: Swatches at 240, 250 and 260 to see the gloss response for the material.

causes.cause: Cooling difference changing surface texture
causes.why: Faster cooling freezes a rougher surface and reads as a colour change.

fixes.action: fan_min_speed and fan_max_speed between the jobs

causes.nextDiagnostic: Swatches at matched fan settings.

symptoms.label: Colour bleed after a filament change
symptoms.hint: Streaks of the previous colour

causes.cause: Purge volume too low for the colour transition
causes.why: Purge requirement scales with the melt-zone volume and with how far the transition goes — dark into light is the worst case.

fixes.action: filament_prime_volume and filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower for dark-to-light steps
Sequence colours light to dark where the model allows

causes.nextDiagnostic: Print a transition swatch and count the layers until the new colour is clean.

causes.cause: Purge temperature too low to shift residue
causes.why: A cold purge leaves film on the melt-zone wall that bleeds for many more layers.

fixes.action: filament_flush_temp toward the higher of the two materials

causes.nextDiagnostic: Same swatch with the flush temperature raised 15 °C.

causes.cause: Melt-zone volume larger than the profile assumes
causes.why: A high-flow hotend holds materially more melt than the stock one the purge default was written for.

fixes.action: Purge volumes by the ratio of melt-zone volumes shown in the Hotends tab

causes.nextDiagnostic: Compare the computed melt-zone volume against the profile's purge volume.

symptoms.label: Supports fuse to the part
symptoms.hint: Supports will not separate cleanly

causes.cause: Support interface gap too small for this material
causes.why: Materials that stay soft longer bond across a gap that works fine for PLA.

fixes.action: top Z distance for support interface
interface line spacing

causes.nextDiagnostic: Support test block at two gaps in the material actually being used.

causes.cause: Insufficient cooling at the interface
causes.why: A hot interface layer welds instead of resting.

fixes.action: fan on interface layers

causes.nextDiagnostic: Compare the same block with interface cooling raised.

causes.cause: Same material used for support where a release material is available
causes.why: On a multi-material machine an interface in a non-bonding material removes the problem rather than tuning around it.

fixes.action: Use a dedicated support or soluble interface material

causes.nextDiagnostic: One interface layer in the release material is usually enough.

symptoms.label: Part knocked loose, spaghetti
symptoms.hint: Print detaches mid-job

causes.cause: Adhesion lost to warping before the knock
causes.why: Almost every knock-off starts as a lifted corner. Fix the lift and the knock disappears.

fixes.action: Work the corner-lift path first
Brim of 5 mm or more as an interim measure

causes.nextDiagnostic: Inspect the base of the detached part for a curled edge.

causes.cause: Small footprint relative to height
causes.why: The overturning moment grows with height while the anchor stays the same size.

fixes.action: Add a brim
acceleration

causes.nextDiagnostic: Reprint with a brim and reduced acceleration as a pair.

causes.cause: Plate contamination in a local patch
causes.why: A fingerprint under one corner is enough.

fixes.action: Full plate wash with detergent

causes.nextDiagnostic: Note whether failures recur at the same plate position.

symptoms.label: Nozzle knocks or scrapes on infill
symptoms.hint: Ticking as the head crosses printed area

causes.cause: Over-extrusion raising the deposited height
causes.why: Each layer lands slightly proud, and the error accumulates until the nozzle touches it.

fixes.action: filament_flow_ratio
Z hop over printed regions as an interim measure

causes.nextDiagnostic: Flow calibration cube. If the top face is proud, this is the cause.

causes.cause: Infill peaks from an aggressive pattern
causes.why: Some patterns cross themselves and stack material at the crossings.

fixes.action: Switch to a non-crossing infill pattern
Ironing or infill combination off while diagnosing

causes.nextDiagnostic: Same part with a different infill pattern.

causes.cause: Curling on the previous layer
causes.why: A curled edge is above nominal height even at correct flow.

fixes.action: overhang_fan_speed
overhang speed

causes.nextDiagnostic: Look at where the knocking happens — over overhangs points at curl, over solid infill points at flow.
